item.description:

item.description:
IMPORTANT: This position is contingent upon contract award. LMD Agency must be awarded the associated government contract and receive authorization to proceed before employment can begin. Candidates may be interviewed and selected in advance but cannot start work until the contract is awarded.

This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 7/30/2026.

LMD is a full-service marketing and branding agency headquartered in Columbia, Maryland, and a woman-owned small business with more than 50 years of history supporting organizations in the public and private sector. The Legislative Analyst supports a federal government client focused on cybersecurity and critical infrastructure security and resilience by providing research, tracking, and administrative support for legislative affairs and public policy activities. The position works under the direction of the Legislative Specialist and is fully remote.

Key responsibilities include: monitoring legislative activity within the U.S. Congress and state legislatures to identify legislation, hearings, and policy developments relevant to the federal client's mission; researching and compiling information on proposed legislation, regulations, executive actions, and public policy initiatives impacting cybersecurity and infrastructure security; assisting in preparing concise summaries, briefing papers, and reports on legislative and policy developments; maintaining trackers for Congressional reporting requirements, engagements, hearings, and legislative activities; supporting the preparation and coordination of Congressional correspondence and responses to inquiries; assisting in producing weekly and annual legislative reports; monitoring Congressional hearings, committee activities, and public policy events and preparing meeting notes; researching and assembling background materials supporting Congressional testimony, QFRs, briefing books, and executive presentations; and maintaining electronic repositories of Congressional testimony, correspondence, and legislative products.

Qualifications: currently holds, or is able to obtain, a DHS Fitness Determination; a bachelor's degree; 1-3 years of professional experience supporting legislative affairs, government relations, public policy, or related analytical functions; demonstrated ability to research legislation, regulations, and public policy issues; and strong research, writing, editing, and analytical skills. Preferred: experience supporting a federal agency, Congressional office, government contractor, or public affairs organization; familiarity with Congress.gov or other legislative tracking tools; and knowledge of cybersecurity, critical infrastructure protection, or national security policy.

Compensation and logistics: the pay range is $66,000-$95,000 per year. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance; short-term disability and life/AD&D insurance; 12 holidays; vacation, sick, and personal leave; parental leave; 401(k) with profit sharing; FSA; and remote work reimbursement.

item.title: Policy Analyst I
item.description:
The Department of Legislative Services (DLS) is the nonpartisan research, legal, and policy analysis staff agency for the Maryland General Assembly. DLS is recruiting Policy Analysts I to work on a nonpartisan basis in three functional areas: Budget Analysis (evaluating operating and capital budgets of state agencies using revenue, spending, and performance data); Fiscal and Policy Notes (analyzing the fiscal, economic, and legal effects of legislation and proposed regulations and preparing official fiscal estimates); and Legislation (drafting legislation and amendments, staffing local legislative delegations, and analyzing proposed state regulations).

Key responsibilities across all three functions include: researching legal and policy issues and developing expertise in specific subject matter areas; conveying quantitative and other analytical findings through written summaries, charts, and visual aids; responding to legislative requests; and presenting findings and recommendations to legislators, committees, task forces, and others in formal and informal settings. The position involves work completed in the Annapolis office and through remote work, with extended hours including evenings and weekends during the legislative session from January to April.

Qualifications: a master's degree or law degree and a demonstrated interest in providing economic, fiscal, legal, or public policy analysis; excellent writing and verbal communication skills; strong analytical abilities including knowledge of basic statistical, mathematical, and financial concepts; competency with standard computer software; the ability to work independently, in teams, and sometimes under extreme time pressure; and availability for extended hours during the legislative session.

Compensation and logistics: the starting salary is $75,000. To apply, email a resume and cover letter to jobs@mga.maryland.gov and include code 02-26. The cover letter should state reasons for interest, any relevant experience, preference for functional assignment, and availability to begin work. An exercise assessing basic writing and mathematical/analytical skills is part of the interview process. Application deadline: July 10, 2026.

item.description:

PK advocates through outreach to Congress, the executive branch, and administrative agencies; filing administrative comments; submitting amicus briefs; hosting public education events; building coalitions; and writing white papers and blog posts. The Government Affairs Policy Counsel/Advocate plays a key role in developing and implementing Public Knowledge's government affairs strategy through advocacy, strategy development, and relationship building in Congress, at federal agencies, and across the public interest field. The position reports to the Director of Government Affairs and is based in Washington, DC.

Qualifications: a college graduate with a passion for public policy and demonstrated interest in the political process and advocacy in the public interest; a law or other graduate degree is a plus; 1-3 years or more of experience with Capitol Hill, federal agencies, or other relevant policy-related experience; familiarity with legislative efforts on technology policy preferred; experience conducting legislative or issue advocacy and developing partnerships; and strong communications skills.

item.title: Energy Policy Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 7/30/2026.

The Cato Institute is a public policy research organization dedicated to the principles of individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace. Its scholars and analysts conduct independent, nonpartisan research on a wide range of policy issues. The Energy Policy Analyst supports the Energy and Environmental Policy Studies department, leading research and advocacy efforts advancing energy freedom, with a focus on consumer-regulated electricity (CRE) at the state and federal levels. The position reports to the Director of Energy and Environmental Policy Studies and is hybrid in Washington, DC. Note: the posting explicitly requires a strong commitment to Cato's libertarian values and an understanding of the free market approach to energy policy — applicants should ensure alignment with the organization's mission before applying.

Key responsibilities include: spearheading new multi-state and federal research and advocacy for energy deregulation; overseeing Cato's efforts to advance consumer-regulated electricity; coordinating among the policy, development, and government affairs teams; engaging outside groups including think tanks and trade associations; writing and presenting testimony before state legislatures; contributing opinion articles to newspapers and speaking on webinars and panels; recruiting new private sector partners; and developing long-term strategy for CRE advocacy and other priorities.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in economics, political science, or a technical field (advanced degree preferred); experience in energy policy with deep knowledge of electricity regulation preferred; an understanding of the free market approach to energy policy; a strong grasp of general economic concepts; and strong writing, communication, and presentation skills. Must have a strong commitment to Cato's libertarian values. Applicants must submit a cover letter detailing expertise in energy policy, philosophical interest in the organization, and a research product or writing sample demonstrating skill in economic analysis. Visa sponsorship is not available.

Compensation and logistics: the salary range is $70,000-$105,000 per year. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; employer HSA contribution; generous vacation and sick days; paid parental leave; employer-provided life and disability insurance; 401(k) employer match; and transit/parking benefits.

item.title: Research Assistant Consultant
item.description:
IMPORTANT: The application deadline for this position is July 2, 2026. Interested applicants should apply immediately via jobs.iadb.org.

The IDB Group is a community of diverse, versatile, and passionate people working to improve lives in Latin America and the Caribbean. The Research Assistant Consultant joins the Poverty Group within the Social Sector, contributing to the design and implementation of high-quality analytical work focused on poverty, inequality, and social inclusion in Latin America and the Caribbean. The role offers hands-on experience with empirical methods, large-scale administrative data, and emerging analytical tools while addressing real-world policy challenges aimed at reducing poverty and promoting inclusive growth in the region. The position is on-site in Washington, DC with occasional telework flexibility.

Key responsibilities include: assisting in the preparation of research papers, policy reports, and presentations; conducting econometric and statistical analyses using Stata (R or Python a plus); analyzing economic and development trends in Latin America and the Caribbean; identifying, compiling, cleaning, and managing large-scale datasets including administrative data; conducting literature reviews and synthesizing existing evidence; contributing to the interpretation of research findings; potentially supporting impact evaluations and field experiments; contributing to the adoption of innovative analytical approaches including AI-assisted coding tools; and collaborating with senior researchers and multidisciplinary teams on rigorous policy-relevant analysis.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in economics, public policy, or a relevant field with a strong quantitative background; 2-5 years of experience in economics of education, labor, migration, gender and diversity, health, or poverty and inequality; experience using household surveys, administrative records, and/or industry surveys; experience with applied micro econometrics, causal inference methods, and program evaluation; proficiency in Spanish and English (spoken and written) required. Citizenship of one of IDB's 48 member countries is required (includes the U.S.).

Compensation and logistics: competitive compensation package including 2 days of leave per month, a monthly health insurance allowance, and relocation and visa assistance when applicable. This is a full-time, 12-month international consultant contract, renewable up to 48 months, based on-site in Washington, DC.

item.description:

Note: this is a limited-term appointment funded through a Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) through December 31, 2026; grant renewal is anticipated and likely but not guaranteed.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in economics, finance, math, or a J.D.; strong analytical and communication skills; familiarity with futures markets, commodities, and trading; familiarity with data analytic tools is a plus; exceptional written and verbal communication skills; ability to prioritize and meet deadline pressure; and knowledge of futures exchange operations, trading, risk management, or regulations.
